readings.title: The Message Seen by the Prophet
readings.subtitle: The formal introduction to the heavy vision delivered to Ḥaḇaqquq.
readings.text: [Habakkuk 1:1] The message which the prophet Ḥaḇaqquq saw.

readings.subsection: The Consequence of a Ceased Torah
readings.title: The Friction of Lawlessness
readings.subtitle: Ḥaḇaqquq witnesses the destructive reality of systemic Ra and a society devoid of right-ruling.
readings.text: [Habakkuk 1:2] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, till when shall <dn>I</dn> cry, and <dn>You</dn> not hear? <dn>I</dn> cry to <dn>You</dn>, “Violence!” and <dn>You</dn> do not save. [3] Why do <dn>You</dn> show <dn>me</dn> wickedness, and cause <dn>me</dn> to see perversity? For ruin and violence are before <dn>me</dn>. And there is strife, and contention arises. [4] Therefore the Torah ceases, and right-ruling never goes forth. For the wrong hem in the righteous, so that right-ruling comes out twisted.

readings.title: YeHoVaH's Instrument of Correction
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH orchestrates geopolitical shifts, raising a bitter nation to execute His precise judgment.
readings.text: [Habakkuk 1:5] <dq>“Look among the nations and see, and be amazed, be amazed! For a work is being wrought in your days which you would not believe if it were told.</dq> [6] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am raising up the Kasdim, a bitter and hasty nation, who is going through the breadth of the earth, to possess dwelling places that are not theirs.</dq> [7] <dq>“They are frightening and fearsome, their right-ruling and their exaltation proceed from themselves.</dq> [8] <dq>“Their horses shall be swifter than leopards, and more fierce than evening wolves. And their horsemen shall charge ahead, and their horsemen come from afar. They fly as the eagle, rushing to eat.</dq> [9] <dq>“All of them come for violence, the direction of their faces is like the east wind, and they gather captives like sand.</dq> [10] <dq>“And they scoff at sovereigns, and princes are a laughing matter to them. They laugh at every stronghold, for they pile up earth and seize it.</dq> [11] <dq>“Then shall he pass on as a wind, and transgress and be guilty, and ascribe this power to his mighty one.”</dq>

readings.subsection: Reconciling Divine Purity with Worldly Chaos
readings.title: The Paradox of the Wicked Net
readings.subtitle: The prophet questions how a perfect Creator can deploy a fundamentally treacherous instrument.
readings.text: [Habakkuk 1:12] Are <dn>You</dn> not from everlasting, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>my</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>my</dn> Set-apart One? <dn>You</dn> do not die! O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>You</dn> have appointed them for right-ruling, O Rock, <dn>You</dn> have established them for reproof. [13] <dn>You</dn>, whose eyes are too clean to see evil, <dn>You</dn> are not able to look on wrong. Why do <dn>You</dn> look on those who act treacherously – keep silent when the wrong devours one more righteous than he? [14] And would <dn>You</dn> make men like fish of the sea, like creeping creatures that have no ruler over them? [15] The wicked foe has pulled all of them up with a hook, caught them in his net, and gathers them in his dragnet. Therefore he rejoices and exults. [16] Therefore he slaughters to his net, and burns incense to his dragnet, for by them is his portion fat and his food is rich. [17] Is he therefore to keep on emptying his net, and killing nations without sparing?

readings.title: Stationed for the Verdict
readings.subtitle: Ḥaḇaqquq readies his mind to receive YeHoVaH's correction and structural perspective.
readings.text: [Habakkuk 2:1] <dn>I</dn> stand at <dn>my</dn> watch, and station <dn>myself</dn> on the watch-tower, and wait to see what <dn>He</dn> says to <dn>me</dn>, and what to answer when <dn>I</dn> am reproved.

readings.title: The Mandate of Emunah
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH declares that true life is sustained by functional trust, leaning fully upon His sound promises.
readings.text: [Habakkuk 2:2] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> answered <dn>me</dn> and said, <dq>“Write the vision and inscribe it on tablets, so that he who reads it runs.</dq> [3] <dq>“For the vision is yet for an appointed time, and it speaks of the end, and does not lie. If it lingers, wait for it, for it shall certainly come, it shall not delay.</dq> [4] <dq>“See, he whose being is not upright in him is puffed up. But the righteous one lives by his steadfastness.</dq>

readings.title: The Reversal of the Usurper
readings.subtitle: Those who extract illicit wealth and load themselves with debt will suffer reciprocal justice, becoming plunder themselves.
readings.text: [Habakkuk 2:5] <dq>“And also, because wine betrays him, a man is proud, and he does not stay at home. Because he enlarges his appetite as She’ol, and he is like death, and is not satisfied, and gathers to himself all nations and heaps up for himself all peoples.</dq> [6] <dq>“Shall not all these lift up a proverb against him, and a mocking riddle against him, and say, ‘Woe to him who increases what is not his! Till when is he to load on himself many pledges’?</dq> [7] <dq>“Do not your creditors rise up suddenly? And those who make you tremble wake up and you be plunder for them?</dq> [8] <dq>“Because you have plundered many nations, all the remnant of the people shall plunder you, because of men’s blood, and doing violence to the land, to the city, and to all who dwell in it.</dq>

readings.title: The Cry of the Very Stones
readings.subtitle: Houses built on the extraction of unjust gain engineer their own ultimate structural shame.
readings.text: [Habakkuk 2:9] <dq>“Woe to him who is getting evil gain for his house, in order to set his nest on high, to escape the clutches of evil!</dq> [10] <dq>“You have counselled shame for your house, to cut off many peoples, and your being is sinning.</dq> [11] <dq>“For a stone from the wall cries out, and a beam from the timbers answers it.</dq>

readings.subsection: The Woe to the Violent Architect
readings.title: Cities Engineered by Blood
readings.subtitle: The labor of the corrupt is destined for the fire, while the Earth will be fundamentally restored with the knowledge of YeHoVaH's esteem.
readings.text: [Habakkuk 2:12] <dq>“Woe to him who builds a town by blood, and establishes a city by unrighteousness!</dq> [13] <dq>“See, it is not from <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts that peoples labour only for fire, and nations weary themselves for naught,</dq> [14] <dq>for the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of <dn>את</dn> the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, as the waters cover the sea!</dq>

readings.title: The Cup of Exposure
readings.subtitle: Those who weaponize vulnerability will be forced to drink from the absolute justice of YeHoVaH's right hand.
readings.text: [Habakkuk 2:15] <dq>“Woe to him who gives drink to his neighbour, pouring out your wineskin, and also making him drunk – in order to look on their nakedness!</dq> [16] <dq>“You shall be filled with shame instead of esteem. Drink, you too, and be exposed as uncircumcised! The cup of the right hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall come around to you, and great shame upon your esteem.</dq> [17] <dq>“For the violence done to Leḇanon is to overwhelm you – and the ravaging of beasts by which you made them afraid – because of men’s blood and the violence to the land, to the city and of all who dwell in it.</dq>

readings.title: The Illusion of Manufactured Authority
readings.subtitle: In the face of the living Creator commanding His universe, the inventions of men are silenced.
readings.text: [Habakkuk 2:18] <dq>“Of what use shall a carved image be? For its maker has carved it: a moulded image and teacher of falsehood! For the maker trusts what he has made: to make dumb idols!</dq> [19] <dq>“Woe to him who says to wood, ‘Awake!’ to silent stone, ‘Arise!’ Is it a teacher? See, it is overlaid with gold and silver, and there is no spirit at all inside it.</dq> [20] <dq>“But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is in <dn>His</dn> set-apart Hĕḵal. Let all the earth be silent before <dn>Him</dn>.”</dq>

readings.section: The Petition for the Final Jubilee
readings.title: A Plea for Divine Intervention
readings.subtitle: Recognizing the severity of YeHoVaH's justice, the prophet asks for restorative mercy in the midst of the years.
readings.text: [Habakkuk 3:1] A prayer of Ḥaḇaqquq the prophet, on Shiḡionoth. [2] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>I</dn> have heard your report, <dn>I</dn> was afraid. O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, renew <dn>Your</dn> work in the midst of the years! Make it known in the midst of the years. In wrath remember compassion.

readings.title: The Infinite Light Unveiled
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH's uncontained essence approaches, shaking ancient foundations and shattering human authority.
readings.text: [Habakkuk 3:3] <dn>Eloah</dn> comes from Tĕman, And the Set-apart One from Mount Paran. Selah. <dn>His</dn> splendour shall cover the heavens, And <dn>His</dn> praise shall fill the earth. [4] And the brightness is as the light, <dn>He</dn> has rays from <dn>His</dn> hand, And there <dn>His</dn> power is hidden. [5] Before <dn>Him</dn> goes pestilence, And a burning flame goes forth at <dn>His</dn> feet. [6] <dn>He</dn> shall stand and measure the earth. <dn>He</dn> shall look and shake the nations. And the ancient mountains are shattered, The age-old hills shall bow. <dn>His</dn> ways are everlasting. [7] <dn>I</dn> saw the tents of Kushan under sorrow, The curtains of the land of Miḏyan tremble.

readings.title: The Physics of Divine Wrath
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH steps through the Earth, deploying natural forces to thresh rebellious nations.
readings.text: [Habakkuk 3:8] Shall <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burn against the rivers? Is <dn>Your</dn> displeasure against the rivers, Is <dn>Your</dn> wrath against the sea, That <dn>You</dn> ride on <dn>Your</dn> horses, <dn>Your</dn> chariots of deliverance? [9] <dn>You</dn> uncover <dn>Your</dn> bow, The oaths of the rod of the Word. Selah. <dn>You</dn> cut through the earth with rivers. [10] The mountains shall see <dn>You</dn>, they tremble. The storm of water shall pass over. The deep shall give forth its voice, It shall lift up its hands. [11] Sun, moon shall stand still in their places. Like light <dn>Your</dn> arrows fly, Like lightning is <dn>Your</dn> glittering spear. [12] <dn>You</dn> step through the earth in rage, <dn>You</dn> thresh the nations in wrath.

readings.subsection: The Strike Against the Serpent's Head
readings.title: The Deliverance of the Right Arm
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH executes salvation for His people, marching to decisively crush the head of the adversary.
readings.text: [Habakkuk 3:13] <dn>You</dn> shall go forth to save <dn>Your</dn> people; to save <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> Anointed. <dn>You</dn> shall smite the head from the house of the wrong, By laying bare from foundation to neck. Selah. [14] <dn>You</dn> shall pierce with his own arrows The head of his leaders. They stormed along to scatter <dn>me</dn>, Rejoicing as if to devour the poor in secret. [15] <dn>You</dn> shall tread the sea with <dn>Your</dn> horses, The foaming of many waters.

readings.title: Absolute Emunah Amidst Collapse
readings.subtitle: Stripped of physical agricultural security, the prophet consciously chooses to rely entirely on YeHoVaH's structural strength.
readings.text: [Habakkuk 3:16] <dn>I</dn> heard, and <dn>my</dn> body trembled, <dn>My</dn> lips quivered at the sound, Rottenness came into <dn>my</dn> bones. And <dn>I</dn> trembled within <dn>myself</dn>, That <dn>I</dn> might rest for the day of distress, To come upon the people who would attack us. [17] Though the fig tree does not blossom, And there is no fruit on the vine, The yield of the olive has failed, And the fields brought forth no food, The flock has been cut off from the fold, And there is no herd in the stalls, [18] Yet <dn>I</dn> exult in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>I</dn> rejoice in the <dn>Elohim</dn> of <dn>my</dn> deliverance. [19] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> the Master is <dn>my</dn> strength. And <dn>He</dn> makes <dn>my</dn> feet like those of deer, And makes <dn>me</dn> walk on <dn>my</dn> high places. To the chief singer with <dn>my</dn> stringed instruments.

readings.title: The Word Given to Tsephanyah
readings.subtitle: The mandate of YeHoVaH descends during the reign of Yoshiyahu, sovereign of Yehuḏah.
readings.text: [Zephaniah 1:1] The word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which came to Tsephanyah son of Kushi, son of Geḏalyah, son of Amaryah, son of Ḥizqiyah, in the days of Yoshiyahu son of Amon, sovereign of Yehuḏah.

readings.title: The Sweeping De-creation
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH initiates an absolute unspooling of creation, targeting those blending His Name with pagan systems.
readings.text: [Zephaniah 1:2] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall snatch away all from the face of the earth,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – [3] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> snatch away man and beast, <dn>I</dn> snatch away the birds of the heavens, and the fish of the sea, and <dn>את</dn> the stumbling-blocks, with <dn>את</dn> the wrong, when <dn>I</dn> shall cut off <dn>את</dn> man from the face of the earth,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [4] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall stretch out <dn>My</dn> hand against Yehuḏah, and against all the inhabitants of Yerushalayim, and cut off <dn>את</dn> every trace of Ba‛al from this place, <dn>את</dn> the names of the idolatrous priests, with the priests,</dq> [5] <dq>and <dn>את</dn> those bowing down to the host of the heavens on the house-tops, and <dn>את</dn> those bowing themselves, swearing by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and swearing by Malkam;</dq> [6] <dq>and <dn>את</dn> those who turn away from following <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and who have not sought <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> or inquired of <dn>Him</dn>.”</dq>

readings.title: Preparing the Sacrifice
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH calls for silence as He prepares to execute precise justice upon corrupt rulers and their violent households.
readings.text: [Zephaniah 1:7] Hush! in the presence of the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. For the day of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is near, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has prepared a slaughter, <dn>He</dn> has set apart <dn>His</dn> invited ones. [8] <dq>“And it shall be, in the day of the slaughter of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that <dn>I</dn> shall punish the rulers and the sons of the sovereign, and all such as are clad in foreign garments.</dq> [9] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall punish on that day all who leap over the threshold, who fill their masters’ houses with violence and deceit.</dq>

readings.title: The Plunder of the Complacent
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH's justice penetrates the merchant centers, dismantling the wealth of those who claim He is inactive.
readings.text: [Zephaniah 1:10] <dq>“And on that day there shall be,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“the sound of a cry from the Fish Gate, and of a howling from the Second Quarter, and of a great crashing from the hills.</dq> [11] <dq>“Howl, you inhabitants of Maḵtĕsh, for all the merchant people shall be silenced, all those weighing out silver shall be cut off.</dq> [12] <dq>“And at that time it shall be, that <dn>I</dn> search Yerushalayim with lamps and punish the men who are settled on their dregs, who say in their heart, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does no good, nor does <dn>He</dn> evil.’</dq> [13] <dq>“And their wealth shall become plunder, and their houses laid waste. And they shall build houses but not inhabit them, and they shall plant vineyards but not drink their wine.”</dq>

readings.title: The Arrival of Wrath
readings.subtitle: The ultimate consequence of lawlessness arrives as a day of profound darkness, dismantling walled defenses.
readings.text: [Zephaniah 1:14] Near is the great day of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, near and hurrying greatly, the noise of the day of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Let the mighty man then bitterly cry out! [15] That day is a day of wrath, a day of distress and trouble, a day of waste and ruin, a day of darkness and gloominess, a day of clouds and thick darkness, [16] a day of a shophar and sounding – against the walled cities and against the corner towers.

readings.title: The Inability of Fiat Power to Save
readings.subtitle: Accumulated silver and gold provide zero shelter against the consuming fire of the Creator's jealousy.
readings.text: [Zephaniah 1:17] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall bring distress on men, and they shall walk like blind men – because they have sinned against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and their blood shall be poured out like dust and their flesh like dung.”</dq> [18] Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them in the day of the wrath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And by the fire of <dn>His</dn> jealousy all the earth shall be consumed, for <dn>He</dn> makes a sudden end of <dn>את</dn> all those who dwell in the earth.

readings.title: An Edict to the Meek
readings.subtitle: Before the decree is executed, YeHoVaH extends an opportunity for the humble to pursue functional harmony and find shelter.
readings.text: [Zephaniah 2:1] Gather together, gather together, O nation without shame, [2] before the law gives birth – the day shall pass on like chaff – before the burning wrath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> comes upon you, before the day of wrath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> comes upon you! [3] Seek <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, all you meek ones of the earth, who have done <dn>His</dn> right-ruling. Seek righteousness, seek meekness, if so be that you are hidden in the day of wrath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Eviction of the Adversaries
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH promises the desolation of the Philistine powers, reserving the land for the restoration of His covenant people.
readings.text: [Zephaniah 2:4] For Azzah is abandoned and Ashqelon laid waste, Ashdoḏ is driven out at noonday and Eqron is uprooted. [5] Woe to the inhabitants of the seacoast, the nation of the Kerĕthites! The word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is against you, O Kena‛an, land of the Philistines, <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall destroy you, so that there is no inhabitant.”</dq> [6] And the seacoast shall be pastures, shepherds’ meadows and enclosures for flocks. [7] And the coast shall be for the remnant of the house of Yehuḏah. They shall feed their flocks on it, at evening they lie down in the houses of Ashqelon. For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn> shall visit them and turn back their captivity.
